newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court hands AIDS-blood file to prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: French court hands AIDS-blood file to prosecutor.

text.p: A French court investigating three former ministers' roles in a scandal of AIDS-tainted blood products has handed the file to a prosecutor, bringing a possible trial one step closer, justice sources said on Monday.

The court is investigating whether ex-prime minister Laurent Fabius and two other former Socialist cabinet ministers delayed importing an American blood test and refused withdrawing tainted blood supplies until France's Pasteur Institute could develop its own screening technique.
The sources said the court's investigators handed the case last week to the state prosecutor who now has three months to draft his conclusions.

The case will then return to the court's investigating committee which will decide whether to order a trial or drop the case. The sources said any trial could take place before a general election scheduled in 1998.
More than 1,250 haemophiliacs were infected by the tainted products in the mid-1980s. More than 400 have since died. The scandal contributed to a rout of the Socialists in 1993 general elections.

The two other former ministers being investigated for alleged poisoning by the Cour de Justice, a special state court established to try ministers for offences committed in office, are ex-social affairs minister Georgina Dufoix and ex-health minister Edmond Herve.

The three have denied the charges and said they acted in good faith on the unanimous advice of experts at the time. Their lawyers have requested experts' reports on how much was known about AIDS at the time.
Four former public health officials were convicted of fraud in 1992 for allowing the continued distribution of the products even though they were known to be tainted.
